txt: (Sings.) Leo, Leo, Easy Leo -- nothing he can't do-ooooo..."
(Sings.) "Container, container, container!"
(Sings.) "Leo, Leo, Leo -- Evrart will be pleased!"
(Sings.) "Plants are happy, boots are shining, every man is fed!"
(Sings.) "Soon, oh soon the green is gone and everything is re-eeed!"
He goes on: "If me missus and me was to have a child I'd be real happy if she turned out like her... But she can't have kids."
He keeps nodding and looking at you with a smile that's too sincere to be clever. Finally he seems to loose some internal struggle and adds: "Them was naked too, that's all I got to say about that."
Leo leans in and whispers: "Them was all naked too. That's all I got to say about that."
Now he's talking about some drunk sawmill owner who... no, he already switched to a prized fishing rod he apparently owned at some point... You know what -- just cut in there with your questions.
The old man whistles and hums a jaunty tune to himself.

They lived on the same street their entire lives -- even dated the same girl on and off for as long I can remember." He chuckles again. "Strange fellows, but mister Martin was always real nice to me in school... I remember once..."
Too late! Leo's mouth is still moving and words are spewing forth... words, words and look -- even more words -- this guy could go on till the end of days.
"... had an arithmetics teacher, Miss Bellows." Leo let's out a little chuckle. "Her real name was Miss Bellams, she was a real pretty lady, but when she got mad..." He starts laughing.
"...but Titus and his boys got into some drunken trouble and Evrart sent them on a nice vacation. For a week or so..." He stops -- but seems eager to tell you more.

"A real pretty lady with a skin like those 'Doux & Sucre' candy bars my missus likes so much. Them are real nice to suckle on once the dinner is done and me and the missus sit down besides the radio."
"Actually, Miss Beaufort is the right-hand man, but she's a lay-dee," a goodhearted chuckle again.

"All kinds of places he visits. Him and his brother both do when they're on a vacation. Right now it's Mr. Evrart's turn to look after the Union, but last year he spent a whole winter in South Safre." He chuckles.

"All the boys liked her if you know what I mean, mister..." He winks at you. "We used to sneak in her yard in the dark and peek through the window. One time we saw Miss Bellows with a fellow. Yes we did, yes we did, mister." He looks for signs of disbelief in your eyes.
"But I can't listen to the radio all the time. There's so much to do around here and I'm always busy keeping things running here. Yes I am, yes I am."

"But Mr. Evrart and his brother always came to help. Once they beat old Noel Becker so bad he needed stitches on his head..." He chuckles again. "Noel never started another fight with anyone after this."
"But she's a real nice girl, grew up in this here neighbourhood, knows everybody and gets along with everyone, real pillar of the community one day, I'm sure."
"Bye bye now!" He returns to his work.
"Container, container, I'll turn you nice and red. Container, container, put the logos on..."
"Container, container, used to be Wild Pines. Container, container now belongs to Evrart!" The tiny man is so engaged in his work he doesn't notice you.
"Doctor Lemaitre said so, and she knows about such things. Been a doctor for almost fifty years, she has..." He sighs and falls silent, watching you meekly with his blue, blue eyes.
"Evrart, Evrart, Evrart, he looks after everyone. Huh... well, hey there!" He smiles. "How can I help you, mister?"
"Guys like Mr. Evrart and Mr. Edgar -- his brother -- are real good guys, made Martinaise what it is today... Mr. Evrart and Mr. Edgar and I went to the same school, we did, when we were boys..."
"He's a Union man through and through. Good guy." He falls silent, hesitating. "He's very calm... laid back. Doesn't do much. Talks to Evrart sometimes."
"Him and his boys stirred something up in town. Probably drank too much and got into a fight or something... I heard Mr. Evrart telling them to take some time off..."
"Honestly. I don't know *what* he does for us, but it must be important because everybody likes him. Yes, they do. I think that's what he does, he makes everyone feel a little better."
"I don't know anyone like this, mister -- maybe he's one of Mr. Evrart's fancy friends. He knows all kinds of fancy people, with suits and perdy carriages." Leo falls silent.

"I guess the boys got a bit too rowdy and had to let out some steam. I don't really know the details. That's just how boys are you know..." Another chuckle. "I haven't been in a fight since I was in middle-school..."
"I mean, I don't personally mind, folks is just folks, you know -- and folks gotta eat..." He doesn't seem to be waiting for you to answer.

"I remember I was the runt of the class." He laughs merrily. "The bigger boys always used to pick on me. You see, I had a bit of a temper back in the day, flew off the handle like nobody's business..."
"I see you are not a Union man, mister. Did you get lost? You're not one of them scabs, are you?" A shadow passes over his kind face.
"I'm like Mr. Evrart's right-hand man, when Mr. Edgar is out of town -- and Mr. *Edgar's* right hand man when Mr. Evrart is away!" He chuckles.
"I'm not sure what a fixer is, but she is a real nice girl. Smart as a whip too." The little guy smiles a disarming smile at you.
"It's true, it's true." he nods. "I've had an eye for helpful people for as long as I remember. I like helpful people, and I like helping helpful people, so what do you need, mister?"
"It's very-very good. Makes a man feel so warm and happy." He shakes his head with a wide smile. "I feel like I could take on Mr. Renaudin's boar-dogs every time the lunch is done."
"Just, some of the other guys don't look too kindly on the scabbing-kind, if you know what I mean, mister."
"Left with the first autumn rains and didn't come back before the trees where green again." The little guy chuckles again.
"Like what, mister?" His wide smile is truly disarming.
"Mr. Edgar is Mr. Evrart's brother. He's looks a bit younger, he does, but a very smart fellow, very smart fellow indeed. He's away on some Union business... Not even in Revachol, they say..."
"Mr. Evrart and Mr. Edgar are real nice guys, mister. You should go talk to Mr. Evrart -- I'm sure you'll be good friends. He's friends with everyone around here." The little guy starts coughing.
"Mr. Evrart doesn't really want me to talk to people about Union guys..." He thinks for a moment. "But who did you want to talk about?"

"Mr. Harry! Boy, old Leo sure was right about you! I knew you was a Union man at heart when I first saw you." He takes a quick breath. "Right as I turned around and looked at you, I said to myself: 'Now that fellow is a union man right there. Through and through.' And I was right, yes I was, yes I was."
"Mr. Martin, yes." Leo nods. "Don't really remember much about him. I was just a boy back then."
"No trouble at all, mister. No trouble at all. It's like that old saying goes -- *wisdom withers if not shared* -- and old Leo is always up for sharing."

"No, I don't think they killed anyone." The little guy shies away from you. "Let's better talk about something else. Titus and his boys do good work, I don't wanna get them in trouble over a little drinking..."
"No, not really." He shrugs and continues merrily: "Mr. Evrart doesn't tell me all the big things. Says I go and tell them to everyone."
"Not everyone is down there of course," he chuckles, "Mr. Evrart is in his office, where he always is, and Jean-Luc is guarding the gate..." He pauses to think.
"Of course, mister. I'm more than happy to be helpful."
"Oh I don't know, mister. They say it's some *chee-mikals*. Most of them have labels on them I think."
"Oh I'm just making some covers for them containers here, yes I am, yes I am... So it's easier for the crane operators to spot them." He waves at the containers towering behind him.

"Oh hey, Mr. Harry!" The little fellow looks happy to see you. "It sure is nice of you to help out Mr. Evrart like you've been doing. He's so awfully busy most days -- he doesn't even eat the turnip porridge me missus sends him every day. She makes it with lots of butter and sliced sausage, she does... It's delicious."

"Oh hey, mister! I knew you'd be back to talk with old Leo here, yes I did, yes I did. It's like Lady Leriche said when she opened a bath house in the basement of my apartment building: *They can only get so far before they're aching to get back*. And lot of folks really did keep coming back..."

"Oh hey, mister! I'm not gonna bother you with a long greeting just like we talked about before. I know you're probably a busy-busy man, being an important police officer and all, and personally I think the more people keeping the peace the better."
"Oh no trouble at all, mister, noooo trouble at all," the little guy affirms merrily.
"Oh no, mister, you've already done so much for the Union. The Union is in your debt, for sure." He nods with a happy smile. "So how can I help you, mister?"
"Oh sure, mister... sure." The little guy nods. "You do that, yes sir."
"Oh that one..." He looks at the container. "That should be empty as far as I know. Lots of containers here have nothing in them. They're just waiting to be loaded up."
"Oh yes, I've been taking special Whirling borscht to the men every day since the strike started." The little guy chuckles merrily.
"Oh yes, born and raised in Iraesh, mister. Mum had to leave my dad after he got a bit violent, took us here to the New New World. I was about ten then, too old to lose my accent then..."
"Oh yes, yes," he replies excitedly. "I leave all kinds of notes for myself. That old head of mine ain't so good at keeping things in no more. I almost forgot about the borscht."
"Oh, I did, mister!" He chuckles again. "Yes I did, yes I did."

"Oh, Lizzy? She is a real sharp tool. Mr. Evrart put her through some fancy school and everything, east of the river. Four years she was gone and when she came back she was all fancy and *law-yerly*."
"Oh, Mr. Evrart is usually in his office, of course." He points to the two joint containers on your right. "But he already left for the day. He always leaves around 22."
"Oh, Mr. Evrart is usually in his office, of course." He points to the two joint containers on your right. "But you gotta be quick if you wanna see him. He leaves around 22."
"Oh, Mr. Evrart is where he always is, in his office, of course." He points to the two joint containers on your right.

"Oh, Titus is a longshoreman through and through, he was born on a boat, they say." The little man rubs a patch on his elbow. "His veins are probably filled with saltwater I tell you, hehehe -- nice friendly sort old Titus is."
"Oh, absolutely, mister." He nods along. "What do you want to know?"
"Oh, mister... I do a lot more than that. I really do most everything around here. Mr. Evrart said many times I'm irreplaceable." He's still smiling, but his voice trembles ever so slightly.
"Oh, most of the guys are down at the gates, keeping the scabs from coming in..." He leans in with a confidential look...
"Oh, the Whirling's cook. He makes it. Them is always talking with Mr. Mañana in that weird language and laughing together. He doesn't speak what we speak, he's from Graad."

"Oh, you want Mr. Evrart, then. He's an awfully nice fellow, he is. Him and his brother are both nice fellows -- they've lived their entire lives in this here neighbourhood." He coughs, then continues immediately...
"Oh... I'm not really supposed to talk about that. That's Union business." He smiles and leans closer.

"Ohh, he's really something..." The little man starts laughing. "He doesn't talk much to me usually, but when he does... I don't really understand most of what he's saying..." He suddenly falls quiet. "Actually, I don't think he would like me running my mouth about him like that."

"Once he said he's a *dragon* to this mob fellow who came picking a fight with some Union men. Heh, I think he really believed Jean-Luc *was* a dragon, because he ran right off. Another time he almost killed another guy, but... I shouldn't talk about that."

"People say us Ubis are up to all sorts of trouble with sheep and other animals and what not -- I just want you to know there was *never* any of that where I come from. No sir. Those are just nasty rumours."
"Sometimes I feel some of the guys don't really get how much I bust my ass for them here, but you guys are all right."
"Sure is mister, sure is!" Leo looks around merrily. "Really livens up the place. Yes it does, yes it does."
"Sure thing, mister. I'm always ready to help out a helpful person such as yourself. Folks have got to help each other out, right?"
"Sure, mister, about what?"
"Sure, mister, absolutely -- I'm always willing to help out nice fellows such as yourself." He smiles his disarming smile and looks you deep in the eye.
"Sure, sure." The small man nods along. "How can I help you?"
"Suuuuure," he stretches the word. "Who did you have in mind?"
"Thank you, mister... Heh! Almost forgot! Mr. Evrart is usually in that container over there." Leo points to his left. "But he already left for the day. He never stays after 22."
"Thank you... Heh! Almost forgot! Mr. Evrart is in that container over there." Leo points to his left. "I got distracted telling the story, but he's in there."
"Thank you... Heh! Almost forgot! Mr. Evrart is usually in that container over there." Leo points to his left. "But he usually leaves around 22, so you gotta be quick if you wanna catch him."
"The night guard? He was a peculiar fellow. Headstrong and proud. We didn't really talk all that much." The little guy looks you in the eye. "He died recently. Somethink with his ticker..."
"The night guard? Oh, he's a peculiar fellow," Leo looks at the guard booth on the wall. "He's the strong silent type you could say."
"Uh... I'd best not... I mean I could, but I don't think Mr. Evrart would like it very much, you better ask him yourself, mister." If anything the ever present smile on Leo's face gets even warmer.
"Uh... sure, mister, what can Leo do for you?" The expression on his wrinkled face says *I really want to help you*.
"Uh... sure, mister," he seems a bit surprised by your abruptness. "What is it?"

"We talk all the time, but I don't really know much about him... He plays pétanque with my old human studies teacher, Mr. Martin down at the plaza. I think he's the only fellow who actually knows old René."
"We're on a *strike* -- the whole union is! You don't have to work when you're on strike. Ha -- we haven't worked for two months now."
"Well thanks a lot, coming from you it means a lot, really." You didn't think it was possible, but the smile becomes even wider.
"Who do you mean, mister?" He's rubbing his nape and looking at you with childlike innocence.
"Yes sure, I'm glad to answer." His benevolent eyes are looking into yours.
"Yes we did, we did, mister." He looks at you and shakes his head. "Indeed we did. Him was a big, big fellow, used to drive the *troyka* near our'ses school and everything."
"Yes, yes, I'm taking it to them. The borscht keeps them happy and in fighting spirits. Makes you all warm inside. They brew it in the Whirling-in-Rags."
"Yes-yes, everybody needs a job and this is mine. I'm Leonard, by the way, Leonard Bellec, but everyone calls me Leo." The little man raises his hand in a welcoming gesture.
